title: Fibrations over a fibered pattern object via its induced pattern
statement: Use the small quasicategories and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the fully scaled categorical patterns and fibered marked objects of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], and their model structures from [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus]. Let $\mathfrak P=(C,S,\{p_\alpha:K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}\to C\})$ be such a pattern, and assume $S$ contains every equivalence edge of $C$. Let $\pi:(Y,T)\to(C,S)$ be a $\mathfrak P$-fibered object. On $Y$ define $\pi^*\mathfrak P$ to have marked base edges $T$, all $2$-simplices scaled, and as specified cones all maps $q:K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}\to Y$ with $\pi q=p_\alpha$ which carry every edge into $T$. This is a small fully scaled categorical pattern. For every marked map $f:(X,U)\to(Y,T)$ over $(C,S)$, the following are equivalent: $f$ is a fibration in $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}$; and $f:(X,U)\to(Y,T)$ is a $\pi^*\mathfrak P$-fibered object. No cocartesian lifts over edges outside $T$ are required.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Remark B.0.27 and Proposition B.2.7, (a) iff (c), printed pp.1469 and 1488-1493, fully scaled case. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this theorem.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak Q=\pi^*\mathfrak P$. The inner-fibration clause for $\pi$ implies that $Y$ is a quasicategory: project an inner horn to $C$, fill it in $C$, and lift that chosen simplex through $\pi$. The marking $T$ contains the degenerate edges. The index set of cones of $\mathfrak Q$ is the disjoint union, over the small set of $\alpha$, of the subsets of $\operatorname{Hom}(K_\alpha^{\triangleleft},Y)$ satisfying the two stated conditions. These are sets in the same universe as the input. Each cone has all its edges marked by construction, and its indexing quasicategory is the original $K_\alpha$. Thus $\mathfrak Q$ is a small fully scaled pattern, including when the family or any $K_\alpha$ is empty.

source.place: Remark B.0.27, induced pattern; direct size and inner-horn checks.

proof.text: We will use the following elementary consequences of the mapping criterion. For any inner fibration $r:E\to B$ of quasicategories, an equivalence edge $u:x\to y$ is $r$-cocartesian: precomposition by $u$ and $r(u)$ has homotopy inverses given by their inverse edges, so both horizontal maps in the criterion's square are equivalences and the square is a homotopy pullback. Conversely, if $u$ is $r$-cocartesian and $r(u)$ is an equivalence, that square implies that $\operatorname{Map}_E(y,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)$ is an equivalence for every $z$. On components, take $z=x$ to obtain $v:y\to x$ with $[v][u]=1_x$; injectivity for $z=y$ gives $[u][v]=1_y$, since their composites with $[u]$ agree. The mapping-composition lemma supplies the two inverse-triangle witnesses, so $u$ is an equivalence. In the square argument write $a:\operatorname{Map}_E(y,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)$ and $b:\operatorname{Map}_B(r(y),r(z))\to\operatorname{Map}_B(r(x),r(z))$ for the horizontal maps, $\rho:\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(r(x),r(z))$ for the right vertical map, and $P(\rho,b)$ for the path-space fiber product. If $b$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, the homotopy-pullback invariance lemma applied to $(\mathrm{id},b,\mathrm{id})$ makes $P(\rho,b)\to P(\rho,\mathrm{id})$ a weak homotopy equivalence, and the path-comparison lemma, for the Kan fibration $\mathrm{id}$, makes the constant-path inclusion $\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)\to P(\rho,\mathrm{id})$ one. The composite of the canonical map $\operatorname{Map}_E(y,z)\to P(\rho,b)$ with the first of these equals the constant-path inclusion composed with $a$, by commutativity of the square. By two-out-of-three, the square is a homotopy pullback if and only if $a$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This gives both directions used above.

source.place: Proof of Proposition B.2.7, equivalence and marking arguments (printed pp.1490-1492); elementary mapping-space proof of the equivalence-edge calculus, usually HTT 2.4.1.5.

proof.text: Assume first that $f$ is a fibration in $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}$. Every generator of $J_{\mathfrak Q}$ becomes a generator of $J_{\mathfrak P}$ after composing its base map with $\pi$. For (A0), (A1), (B0), and (C0), the required edges of the base map lie in $T$, hence map into $S$; (C1) has no marking restriction. A cone of $\mathfrak Q$ used by (B1) or (C2) projects to its specified $p_\alpha$, so these are also generators of the indicated type for $\mathfrak P$. All triangle conditions are automatic because both patterns are fully scaled. By [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-generators], these images are trivial cofibrations of $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}$. A square for a generator of $J_{\mathfrak Q}$ against the terminal arrow $(X,U)\to(Y,T)$ is precisely the resulting square against $f$ over $C$. The model weak factorization system fills it. The generator recognition theorem for $\mathfrak Q$ therefore says that $f$ is $\mathfrak Q$-fibered.

source.place: Proposition B.2.7, (a) implies (c), printed p.1491; the special case of B.2.9 is checked generator by generator instead of invoked as a new lemma.

proof.text: For the converse assume $f:(X,U)\to(Y,T)$ is $\mathfrak Q$-fibered, and put $q=\pi f$. First prove that $(X,U)\to(C,S)$ is $\mathfrak P$-fibered. Given a generator $j:D\to E$ of $J_{\mathfrak P}$ and a marked map $D\to X$ over its fixed base map $E\to C$, compose to $Y$. Since $Y$ is $\mathfrak P$-fibered, fill this square to a marked map $v:E\to Y$. Now $j$, with base map $v$, belongs to $J_{\mathfrak Q}$: the sharp edges in the target of (A0), (A1), and (B0) ensure the requisite base edges lie in $T$; the distinguished edge $01$ in (C0) does the same; (C1) has no restriction. In (B1) the whole cone maps into $T$, and its projection is $p_\alpha$, so $v$ is a specified cone of $\mathfrak Q$. In (C2) the distinguished last-vertex cone $\{n\}\star K_\alpha$ is sharp in $E$, so its restriction under $v$ is such a specified cone. All 2-simplices are scaled. Fill the resulting generator square through $f$. This gives $E\to X$ over $C$ for every $j$, hence the generator recognition theorem makes $X$ $\mathfrak P$-fibered. In particular it gives exactly the marking $U$ of $q$-cocartesian edges over $S$, and both cone conditions of the definition; neither condition for an empty cone has been discarded.

source.place: Proposition B.2.7, (c) implies (b), printed pp.1491-1493; express the composition argument through the seven generators of B.1.1 and B.1.6.

proof.text: The underlying $f:X\to Y$ is an isofibration. It is an inner fibration by $\mathfrak Q$-fibrancy. Since $Y$ is a quasicategory, the inner-horn argument of step 1 also makes $X$ a quasicategory. For an equivalence $e:f(x)\to y$ in $Y$, its image $\pi(e)$ is an equivalence (apply the simplicial map to the inverse witnesses), hence belongs to $S$. Step 2 makes $e$ $\pi$-cocartesian, so the exact-marking clause for the $\mathfrak P$-fibered object $Y$ puts $e$ in $T$. The lifting clause for the $\mathfrak Q$-fibered map $f$ gives an $f$-cocartesian lift $\widetilde e$ with source $x$. Step 2 makes $\widetilde e$ an equivalence because $f(\widetilde e)=e$ is one. This is exactly equivalence-edge lifting with prescribed source, without requiring any lift of an edge outside $T$.

source.place: Proposition B.2.7, (c) implies (b), equivalence lifting; fully scaled case and S containing equivalences.

proof.text:
Let $i:(A,M_A)\hookrightarrow(B,M_B)$ be an arbitrary trivial cofibration of $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}$, and take a square with top map $a:A\to X$ and bottom map $g:B\to Y$ against $f$. Step 4 and the model's fibrant-object identification imply that $X\to(C,S)$ lifts $i$, giving a marked $h':B\to X$ over $C$ with $h'i=a$. The maps $fh'$ and $g$ agree on $A$. Set
$$D=(A\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp)\amalg_{A\times(\partial\Delta^1)^\sharp}(B\times(\partial\Delta^1)^\sharp).$$
Map $D$ to $Y$ by the constant $fa$ on the first summand, by $fh'$ at endpoint $0$, and by $g$ at endpoint $1$. These agree on the intersection. Its inclusion into $B\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp$ is the pushout product of $i$ with the point-model cofibration $(\partial\Delta^1)^\sharp\hookrightarrow(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, hence is a trivial pattern cofibration by the marked enriched axiom. Since $Y$ is fibrant, extend to a marked map $G:B\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp\to Y$ over $C$. Thus $G$ runs from $fh'$ to $g$ and is constant $fa$ on $A$.

source.place: Proposition B.2.7, (b) implies (a), printed pp.1490-1491: first extension and the relative marked cylinder; use the stated full pushout-product axiom.

proof.text:
We check the equivalence needed to lift this homotopy with the boundary fixed. By [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products], restriction
$$\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(B,Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(A,Y)$$
is a Kan fibration between Kan complexes. Its degreewise fiber $V$ at the vertex $fa$ is Kan: a horn in the fiber is filled by that fibration over the constant simplex at $fa$. The maps $fh',g$ are vertices of $V$, and $G$ is an edge of $V$. Every edge in the Kan complex $V$ is an equivalence by [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration], so it has the two inverse-triangle witnesses in the stated definition of equivalence. These witnesses remain in $V$, so remain constant on $A$. Put
$$Q=\operatorname{Fun}(A,X)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Fun}(B,Y).$$
The map $V\to Q$ sends a simplex $H$ to the pair consisting of the constant simplex at $a$ and the underlying $H$. Consequently the pair $(1_a,G)$ is an equivalence edge in $Q$, with source $(a,fh')$ and target $(a,g)$; its inverse witnesses are the images of those in $V$.

source.place: Proposition B.2.7, relative equivalence between the two extensions, printed p.1491; explicit fixed-boundary inverse witnesses using B.1.14.

proof.text:
Apply the exponential-corner theorem to the isofibration $f$ of step 5 and the underlying monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow B$. It says that $Q$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(B,X)$ are quasicategories and that
$$R:\operatorname{Fun}(B,X)\longrightarrow Q,\qquad h\longmapsto(h|_A,fh)$$
is an isofibration. Since $R(h')=(a,fh')$, lift the equivalence edge $(1_a,G)$ of step 7 to an equivalence edge $H:h'\to h$. Its target satisfies $hi=a$ and $fh=g$ exactly, and $H|_A$ is the constant edge at $a$. Moreover $qH=\pi G$ is the constant transformation at the prescribed base map $B\to C$. The pointwise equivalence criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] implies that every vertex component $H_b$ is an equivalence in $X$.

source.place: Proposition B.2.7, homotopy lifting in the proof of (b) implies (a), printed p.1491; use the existing exponential-corner theorem to impose the boundary exactly.

proof.text: It remains to check that $h$ preserves all marked edges of $B$, not merely those of $A$. For a marked edge $e:b\to b'$ of $B$, the map $H$ on $e\times\Delta^1$ gives two triangles with common diagonal $d$, expressing $d$ as $H_{b'}h'(e)$ and as $h(e)H_b$. By step 2 the equivalences $H_b,H_{b'}$ are $q$-cocartesian. The edge $h'(e)$ is marked, hence $q$-cocartesian by step 4. Apply the composition-and-cancellation assertion twice: first $d$ is $q$-cocartesian because both $h'(e)$ and $H_{b'}$ are; then $h(e)$ is $q$-cocartesian because $H_b$ and $d$ are. Finally $q h(e)=\pi g(e)$ belongs to $S$, since $g$ preserves markings and $\pi(T)\subseteq S$. The exact-marking clause for $X$ now gives $h(e)\in U$. Thus $h$ is the required marked diagonal. Since $i$ was any trivial cofibration, the model weak factorization system makes $f$ a fibration of $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}$. Together with step 3 this proves the equivalence. The argument has imposed cocartesian lifting only over $T$, as required.

source.place: Proposition B.2.7, last marking check for (b) implies (a), printed p.1491; two triangles spell out the check for marked edges of B (the printed proof says A here).

proof_origin.place: Auxiliary marked-operadic foundation for proof paragraph 2, finite-coefficient mapping-complex comparison. Complete argument adapted from Higher Algebra, Remark B.0.27 and Proposition B.2.7, read online; the literature archive lacks HA.
